import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate total spending on all products
df['TotalSpending'] = df[[
    'MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts',
    'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds'
]].sum(axis=1)

# Create a categorical feature indicating presence of children
# 'Has Children' if Kidhome > 0 or Teenhome > 0, otherwise 'No Children'
df['Children_Status'] = ((df['Kidhome'] > 0) | (df['Teenhome'] > 0)).astype(str)
df['Children_Status'] = df['Children_Status'].replace({'True': 'Has Children', 'False': 'No Children'})

# Filter out rows with NaN in Income and extreme income outliers for better visualization
df_filtered = df.dropna(subset=['Income'])
# Filter incomes greater than a reasonable threshold (e.g., 200,000) to avoid compressing the main data
df_filtered = df_filtered[df_filtered['Income'] < 200000]

# Set a clean seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df_filtered,
    x='Income',
    y='TotalSpending',
    hue='Children_Status',
    palette={'No Children': '#4CAF50', 'Has Children': '#FFC107'}, # Green for no children, Amber for children
    alpha=0.7,
    s=70, # Size of the points
    edgecolor='w', # White edge for points
    linewidth=0.5
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Customer Total Spending vs. Income by Family Status', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold')
plt.xlabel('Income', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Spending on Products', fontsize=14)

# Customize legend
plt.legend(title='Family Status', title_fontsize='13', fontsize='11', loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

# Add grid and improve layout
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
